# Fixture inventory

`core/` is independently authored deterministic Oracle MySQL data and a PostgreSQL `public.users` sentinel. It covers relational keys, empty/keyless tables, exact decimal/unsigned/binary values, UTF-8, temporal duration, zero dates and text NUL. Invalid rows live separately so normal acceptance can select the supported clean tables. The harness records source SQL SHA-256 hashes and runs independent SQL assertions.

[upstream-manifest.json](upstream-manifest.json) classifies **all 13 selected MySQL `.load` files**, every MySQL-containing parser/AST case in the selected Clojure suites, the unified suite's 19 SQL assertions and supplemental seed files. It records upstream commit, exact file hashes, license/provenance and new case IDs. A classification is a compatibility decision; `implementation_status: pending` explicitly means the new case has not passed yet. Workers must register the eventual behavioral test and evidence before changing it to passed.

Run `rtk run 'python3 tests/support/fixture_manifest.py'` from my2pg to check inventory completeness and immutable snapshot hashes; release tests need no sibling checkout. Add `--upstream` to independently compare the snapshot against the read-only upstream revision. Legacy load files contain only upstream synthetic example credentials and are importer input fixtures, never automatically executed. External Sakila/F1DB data are optional provisioned corpora; their download/runtime evidence and notices must accompany any later copied dataset.

The reviewed source fixtures are preserved under `upstream/` at their original paths, with `LICENSE` and `DATASET-NOTICES.md` copied from the pinned pgloader checkout. Parser files are retained only as source input/provenance; they are not executable Clojure dependencies. Their excluded-source examples remain negative reference material. Sakila/F1DB datasets themselves are not copied. This manifest does not grant a new license for those datasets.

The disposable TLS fixture uses a per-run CA and localhost server identity. PostgreSQL role `my2pg client` requires TLS, a trusted matching client certificate and its synthetic password; ordinary fixture accounts keep password authentication. The harness verifies 14 seed/catalog assertions, including parsed client-certificate HBA rules. Trusted wrong-CN, untrusted-CA and historically expired client identities support production authentication rejection tests; wrong-host and expired server identities support scoped protocol peers. Keys, connection URLs and generated CA state live only in ignored private run artifacts. These certificates are generated locally for tests.
